newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Attorney files civil suit against Sears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Attorney files civil suit against Sears.

text.p: The U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts said Thursday his office filed a civil complaint against Sears, Roebuck and Co to stop allegedly "fradulent" debt collection activities.
U.S. Attorney Donald Stern also said a federal investigation into Sears's practice of collecting debts from its once-bankrupt credit card customers was continuing.
"The federal investigation is continuing," Stern said.

Sears has agreed to an entry of a preliminary injunction which would halt the practice nationwide and has agreed to an audit of debtors who have been victimized by its conduct, the U.S. Attorney's office said. The government also intends to later seek restitution from Sears for debtors victimized by the practice, and civil penalties, he said.

As a matter of company policy, Sears misled many of its bankrupt credit card holders to believe they had to repay their debts to the company, even though those bills had been nullified by a bankruptcy court, court papers alleged.

The massive retailer allegedly conducted an "intentinoal and deliberate practice" to obtain agreements, called reaffirmations, to collect from its credit card debtors during their bankruptcy, Stern's office said.
"Sears's practice has had the effect of thwarting the entire purpose of a bankruptcy, which is to give debtors a fresh start," Stern said in a press release.
In Massachusetts alone, Sears has admitted to collecting from at least 2,733 such debtors, Stern's office said.

Sears has agreed to complete its ongoing review to identify all debtors affected by its conduct from January 1992 to the present and will provide the U.S. Attorney's office with status reports every two weeks, Stern's office said.
